AI.conclusion: The matching is consistent and provides valuable insights, though it fails to simultaneously model all five CMS azimuthal observables.

title: Time lags as proxy of spectral evolution in gamma-ray bursts
comment: 13 pages, 6 figures, 4 tables, Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics (A&A)
summary: Positive lags in gamma-ray bursts (GRBs), where hard photons anticipate softer ones, provide a unique window into the temporal evolution of their prompt emission. Negative lags, when hard photons are delayed, are instead more enigmatic to interpret. Disentangling the effects that produce both kinds of lags is critical for identifying the physical mechanisms at work in the prompt and early afterglow phases of GRBs. We investigate the potential of time lags for distinguishing different emission components at different energy bands. Using data from the Fermi Gamma-ray Burst Monitor (GBM) and the LAT Low Energy(LLE) technique, we perform a time-resolved joint spectral analysis in the range 10 keV-100 MeV for two exceptionally bright bursts, GRB 160625B and GRB 190114C. Time lags between the lowest-energy band (10-100 keV) and progressively higher-energy bands up to 30-100 MeV were computed across their distinct emission episodes via the cross-correlation function. For GRB 160625B, the spectra are described by a single component with clear hard-to-soft evolution, and the time lags are always positive. Analysis of the high-energy exponential cutoff, likely originating above the photosphere, yields bulk Lorentz factor estimates of $Γ\sim 120-250$. GRB 190114C exhibits negative lags in the 30-100 MeV band, coinciding with a delayed high-energy powerlaw component that dominates the LLE range after ~2.5 s. Comparison with multi-wavelength observations shows some compatibility with the early afterglow, though its origin remains open, leaving room for external shocks or internal dissipation. Time lags are effective diagnostic tools for the spectral evolution of GRBs: positive lags trace the softening of the prompt emission, whereas negative lags indicate the appearance of a new, independent high-energy spectral component.

AI.tldr: The study analyzes time lags in gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) to understand emission mechanisms, revealing distinct behaviors in two bursts that aid in diagnosing spectral evolution.
AI.motivation: Understanding the temporal evolution of prompt emissions in GRBs and disentangling the effects that lead to both positive and negative lags is essential for identifying underlying physical mechanisms.
AI.method: Utilized data from the Fermi Gamma-ray Burst Monitor to perform time-resolved joint spectral analysis on two bright bursts, calculating time lags across energy bands via the cross-correlation function.
AI.result: GRB 160625B exhibits only positive lags with hard-to-soft evolution, whereas GRB 190114C shows negative lags with a delayed high-energy power-law component, indicating different underlying emission processes.
AI.conclusion: Time lags are valuable diagnostic tools, with positive lags reflecting the softening of prompt emissions and negative lags suggesting the emergence of independent high-energy components.

title: Efficient Magic State Cultivation for $\sqrt{T}$ Gates
summary: Recently, experimental and theoretical quantum error correction methodology has seen remarkable breakthroughs. In particular, magic state cultivation has been shown to simplify magic-state preparation and make it feasible for near-term devices. However, recent research on magic state cultivation has focused primarily on the cultivation of $T\left| + \right>_L$. Only a few other magic state cultivation methods beyond $T\left| + \right>_L$ have been investigated. Here, we generalize phase kickback checks for magic states at arbitrary Clifford hierarchy levels in specific codes. We provide an example of cultivation of $\sqrt{T}\left| + \right>_L$ in the doubled color code and the corresponding escape strategy using lattice surgery from the color code to large rotated surface codes. Using state vector simulation for un-grown cultivation, we observe a strong consistence between $S\left| + \right>_L$ and $\sqrt{T}\left| + \right>_L$ cultivation's performance on the doubled color code. Finally, we discuss the application of the corresponding $\sqrt{T}\left| + \right>_L$ cultivation, incorporating the STAR architecture and $T$ gates, for early fault-tolerant quantum computing and its potential to shorten gate synthesis in the fully fault-tolerant quantum computing era.

AI.tldr: This paper explores generalization techniques for magic state cultivation beyond the commonly studied $T| + \rangle_L$ state, particularly focusing on the $\sqrt{T}| + \rangle_L$ state within doubled color codes and its implications for fault-tolerant quantum computing.
AI.motivation: To extend the current understanding and methods of magic state cultivation beyond the prevalent $T| + \rangle_L$ state, in order to enhance fault-tolerant quantum computing capabilities.
AI.method: The authors generalize phase kickback checks for arbitrary Clifford hierarchy levels and present a cultivation method for $\sqrt{T}| + \rangle_L$ using doubled color codes, along with strategies utilizing lattice surgery to shift to larger rotated surface codes.
AI.result: State vector simulations demonstrate the strong performance correlation between $S| + \rangle_L$ and $\sqrt{T}| + \rangle_L$ cultivation on doubled color codes, indicating effective error correction capabilities.
AI.conclusion: The $\sqrt{T}| + \rangle_L$ cultivation strategy is potentially beneficial for early fault-tolerant quantum computing, especially in reducing gate synthesis times when integrated with architectures like STAR and employing $T$ gates.

title: Multiplicity-dependent forward jet production in proton-nucleus collisions
summary: Forward jet production in proton--nucleus collisions probes a dilute projectile scattering from a dense small-$x$ nuclear gluon field, while the charged-particle multiplicity inside the jet probes the final-state cascade in the jet cone. We develop a factorization framework for single-inclusive forward jets with an internal multiplicity measurement by combining the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) description of the production process with soft-collinear effective theory (SCET) semi-inclusive jet functions. The construction preserves the inclusive limit exactly: at zero multiplicity weight it reduces to the known inclusive next-to-leading order (NLO)/resummed CGC forward-jet cross section. We define the multiplicity-measured jet operator in a CGC background, formulate the matching that separates PDF, BK/JIMWLK, Sudakov, SiJF, and multiplicity-evolution radiation, and identify the Wilson-line resolution mechanism through which saturation can modify the internal multiplicity evolution. The resulting framework shows that high-multiplicity forward jets are sensitive both to the quark/gluon mixture generated by the CGC production kernel and to finite-$Q_s$ corrections when an early in-cone splitting is resolved by the target. A baseline numerical implementation validates the factorized structure and illustrates the resulting multiplicity-conditioned nuclear modification.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a factorization framework for analyzing forward jets in proton-nucleus collisions, accounting for both production and internal multiplicity.
AI.motivation: To understand the dynamics of forward jet production and internal multiplicity in proton-nucleus collisions, leveraging the interplay between CGC and SCET frameworks.
AI.method: Combining the Color Glass Condensate (CGC) framework with soft-collinear effective theory (SCET) to develop a factorization approach for inclusive forward jets with internal multiplicity measurements.
AI.result: High-multiplicity forward jets reveal sensitivity to the quark/gluon composition from CGC and to finite-$Q_s$ corrections, with a structure validated by numerical implementation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed framework successfully connects jet production with internal multiplicity evolution, providing insights into nuclear modifications in high-energy collisions.

title: The link between obscured accretion and mildly relativistic precessing jets
comment: Accepted for publication in MNRAS. Link to published version of Fender & Motta (Nature Astronomy, 2025) on which this builds, is here: https://www.nature.com/articles/s41550-025-02665-w
summary: We have recently shown evidence that the most relativistic jets (with Lorentz factor >2) from stellar-mass black holes in X-ray binary systems may be locked to a fixed axis, likely the spin axis of the black hole. Slower, mildly relativistic jets (with velocities typically ~ 0.3c) are often seen to precess and can be associated with both neutron stars and black holes. In this paper we demonstrate an additional clear link between highly obscured systems and these lower-velocity, precessing jets. We speculate that this link may be due to mass-loading of the jets close to their launch sites, since these obscured systems are likely to be examples of (sometimes persistent, other times transient) super-Eddington accretion. The fastest relativistic jets are now seen to be both locked to a fixed direction, likely the black hole spin axis, and to be launched in low-density environments, while jets launched in dense environments are generally slower and very likely to precess.

AI.tldr: This paper establishes a connection between highly obscured systems and lower-velocity, precessing jets in black holes and neutron stars, suggesting that mass loading from super-Eddington accretion influences jet properties.
AI.motivation: To explore the relationship between the dynamics of relativistic jets from black holes and neutron stars, particularly in relation to their launch environments and orientations.
AI.method: The paper analyses observational data on jet velocities, precession, and environmental conditions of stellar-mass black holes and neutron stars, correlating these findings with the degree of obscuration and accretion rates.
AI.result: Demonstrated a clear link between obscured systems and slower, precessing jets, indicating that environmental density plays a critical role in jet characteristics.
AI.conclusion: Relativistic jets are directionally fixed when launched in low-density conditions, while jets in dense environments are slower and tend to precess, highlighting the influence of mass loading and accretion dynamics.

title: Experimental implementation of continuous-variable QAOA on a quad-rail lattice cluster state
summary: We experimentally demonstrate the continuous-variable quantum approximate optimization algorithm (CV-QAOA) for multi-variable problems and multiple QAOA depths using a measurement-based CV quantum computing platform on a quad-rail lattice (QRL) cluster state. We propose a systematic method to map arbitrary quadratic cost functions onto the QRL architecture and examine the resulting construction in settings involving up to 100 modes. Using the programmable platform, we prepare the CV-QAOA ansatz and optimize the variational parameters via Bayesian optimization. We then investigate the performance on quadratic optimization problems and observe that increasing the depth from 1 to 2 improves performance, whereas further increases yield only limited gains. In contrast, numerical simulations under idealized conditions, assuming an infinite number of measurement shots and gradient-based optimization, indicate that the performance of CV-QAOA can improve with increasing depth, suggesting that the experimentally observed limitations primarily arise from noise accumulation and classical optimization challenges. This work provides an experimental demonstration of CV-QAOA on a programmable CV platform and establishes a foundation for future developments of variational quantum algorithms in CV systems.

AI.tldr: Experimental demonstration of the CV-QAOA on a quad-rail lattice cluster state shows performance improvements with depth but limited gains beyond depth 2; suggests challenges from noise and optimization.
AI.motivation: To advance continuous-variable quantum computation by demonstrating the CV-QAOA for multi-variable problems using a novel architecture.
AI.method: Implemented CV-QAOA on a quad-rail lattice cluster state, mapping quadratic cost functions, optimizing parameters with Bayesian methods, and testing various QAOA depths.
AI.result: Performance improves from QAOA depth 1 to 2, but further depth increases yield diminishing returns; noise and optimization limitations noted.
AI.conclusion: This work establishes a foundation for the development of variational quantum algorithms in continuous-variable quantum systems.

title: Resolving SLX 1744-299 and SLX 1744-300 in the hard X-ray band: implications for their ultracompact nature
comment: 10 pages, 7 figures. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics
summary: Persistent, low-luminosity low-mass X-ray binaries (LMXBs) offer a unique opportunity to study accretion in this poorly understood regime, as well as to unveil new members of the ultracompact X-ray binary (UCXB) family, characterised by orbital periods ($P_{\rm orb}$) shorter than $\sim 80$ min. We report on a NuSTAR archival observation that, for the first time above 10 keV, spatially resolves the Galactic Centre pair SLX 1744$-$299 and SLX 1744$-$300. We find SLX 1744$-$300 to be slightly brighter, with a flux ratio of $\sim 1.15$, increasing to $\sim 1.3$ when extrapolated to 0.5$-$10 keV. Both the timing (root-mean-square variability) and spectral properties (well described in both cases by a thermal Comptonisation model) indicate that the systems were in the hard state. The two sources, however, display markedly different behaviour throughout the observation. SLX 1744$-$299 shows a gradual flux decline consistent with a decrease in the mass-accretion rate, whereas SLX 1744$-$300 remains steady but exhibits two short-recurrence Type-I X-ray bursts indicative of mixed H/He burning. Combining our results with previously reported upper limits on the distance, we derive low persistent X-ray luminosities of $L_{\rm X}\lesssim 1.1\times10^{36}$ erg s$^{-1}$ and $L_{\rm X}\lesssim 2.6\times10^{36}$ erg s$^{-1}$ (3$-$78 keV) for SLX 1744$-$299 and SLX 1744$-$300, respectively. The corresponding mass-accretion rates, when compared with the critical values from the disc instability model, favour $P_{\rm orb}\lesssim 90$ min and $P_{\rm orb}\lesssim 105-155$ min. Although both limits are formally compatible with the UCXB regime, the case of SLX 1744$-$299 appears significantly more compelling, also considering the previously reported intermediate-duration burst.

AI.tldr: This study examines low-luminosity low-mass X-ray binaries SLX 1744$-$299 and SLX 1744$-$300 at the Galactic Centre using a NuSTAR observation, revealing their differing behaviors and contributions to understanding ultracompact X-ray binaries.
AI.motivation: To explore accretion processes in low-luminosity low-mass X-ray binaries and identify new ultracompact X-ray binaries.
AI.method: Utilized a NuSTAR archival observation to analyze the spectral and timing properties of SLX 1744$-$299 and SLX 1744$-$300.
AI.result: Findings indicate that SLX 1744$-$300 is slightly brighter than SLX 1744$-$299, with the former showing steady flux and Type-I bursts, while the latter displays a gradual flux decline.
AI.conclusion: Both sources have luminosities consistent with ultracompact X-ray binary characteristics, particularly SLX 1744$-$299, which suggests a more convincing scenario for being an UCXB.

title: Analytical performance evaluation of quantum radar architectures: From single-photon to entangled-noise radars
comment: This article has been published in AVS Quantum Science. \c{opyright} AIP Publishing. The final published version is available at DOI: https://doi.org/10.1116/5.0316803
summary: This article presents a comprehensive analysis of two classes of quantum radars, including quantum direct-detection and quantum-entangled noise radars. In the first case, inspired by the well-established concept of single-photon LiDARs, we investigated the performance of single-photon radars, in which state-of-the-art single microwave-photon detectors are employed to enhance the detection sensitivity and enable the detection of weaker signals. We derived analytical expressions for the maximum detection range of both classes of quantum radars in terms of the Lambert W function, by considering all relevant system, target, and environmental parameters. Our formulation facilitates direct comparison of noise radars with direct-detection radars and suggests that a quantum-entangled noise radar can be regarded as an enhanced direct-detection radar with an effective threshold signal-to-noise ratio. Furthermore, we applied this framework to classical-correlated noise radars and defined the parameter range enhancement factor (REF) to quantify the superiority of quantum-entangled noise radars over their classical counterparts. Moreover, we introduced a rule-of-thumb for approximating the REF. We also examined the influence of limitations imposed by various microwave detection technologies. Our analysis shows that the conventional antennas limit the potential benefits of quantum-entangled noise radar systems. We also demonstrated that the optimal detection method for these radars is a microwave detector based on a quantum transducer combined with a single optical-photon detector. We showed that, with the current technology, implementing a quantum-entangled noise radar with the maximum detection range on the order of few kilometers is possible. Finally, we explored the potential applications of quantum-entangled noise radars.

AI.tldr: The article analyzes quantum direct-detection and quantum-entangled noise radars, deriving performance metrics and comparing their detection capabilities.
AI.motivation: To enhance radar detection sensitivity and range using emerging quantum technologies.
AI.method: Analytical expressions for detection range were derived using the Lambert W function, comparing quantum and classical radar technologies, and defining a parameter range enhancement factor (REF).
AI.result: Quantum-entangled noise radars outperform classical systems, with a proposed optimal detection method achieving detection ranges of a few kilometers.
AI.conclusion: The study highlights the advantages and practical applications of quantum-entangled noise radars, suggesting enhancements over classical systems.

title: DarkAgents
summary: We present DarkAgents: a multi-agent system that leverages the reasoning and code-generation capabilities of large language models (LLMs), together with deterministic tested human-written code, to build orchestrated pipelines for theoretical astroparticle physics research. While related approaches have been proposed in collider physics and cosmology, DarkAgents targets the specific challenges of this domain, such as model building, complex pipeline computations, multiple constraints and assumption auditing. The framework can be powered by different agentic command-line tools, including Mistral's, Anthropic's, OpenAI's and local LLMs via Ollama. As first implementation, we apply DarkAgents to the study of cosmological first order transitions, starting from a classically scale-invariant particle-physics model and ending with the fit to the NANOGrav nanohertz gravitational-waves spectrum. DarkAgent-PT provides as output i) the best-fit values of model parameters, ii) their existing experimental and observational constraints, iii) an audit report of the assumptions and priors entering both i) and ii), of particular relevance for astroparticle physics. Our test runs identify inconsistencies in some fits in the literature and produce novel ones based on the dissipative bulk-flow GW template. The code is publicly available at https://github.com/PhysicsZandi/DarkAgents.

AI.tldr: DarkAgents is a multi-agent system for astroparticle physics that integrates LLMs and human-written code to analyze cosmological phenomena, particularly gravitational waves, revealing inconsistencies in literature and offering new insights.
AI.motivation: To address specific challenges in theoretical astroparticle physics, such as model building and assumption auditing, using advanced AI capabilities alongside existing code.
AI.method: Utilizing a multi-agent system that combines the reasoning power of LLMs with deterministic human-written code to create orchestrated research pipelines.
AI.result: The application of DarkAgents to cosmological transitions produced best-fit model parameters, audits of constraints, and identified inconsistencies in existing literature, alongside novel findings based on gravitational wave templates.
AI.conclusion: DarkAgents facilitates enhanced analysis in astroparticle physics, providing valuable outputs for the field and improving theoretical model assessment.

title: Floquet analysis of coherence in periodically driven diamond NV ensemble systems
summary: High-density nitrogen-vacancy (NV) ensembles are promising platforms for solid-state quantum sensing, but their performance is limited by dipolar interactions and inhomogeneous dephasing. Periodic decoupling sequences such as Waugh-Huber-Haeberlen (WAHUHA) can extend the observed stroboscopic decay time. However, it remains unclear that a longer effective dephasing time yield improved magnetic-field sensitivity. Here, we show that WAHUHA control increases the effective inhomogeneous dephasing time of a dense NV ensemble from $T_2^\ast$ of 0.9 $μ$s to $T_{2,eff}^\ast$ of 31 $μ$s, while producing little improvement in dc magnetic-field sensitivity. Using detuning-resolved stroboscopic spectroscopy and finite-pulse Floquet analysis, we show that the long-lived signal arises from phase wrapping and quasi-energy branch folding of the one-cycle unitary. These effects reshape the stroboscopic spectrum and suppress the detuning-to-phase transduction slope, $dΦ/dΔ$, which governs the dc magnetic-field response. Our results demonstrate that, under periodic driving, an extended effective dephasing time does not necessarily translate into enhanced dc sensitivity and establish finite-pulse Floquet analysis as a practical framework for evaluating coherence in spin ensembles.

AI.tldr: Periodic decoupling with WAHUHA enhances the effective dephasing time of NV ensembles but does not improve magnetic-field sensitivity.
AI.motivation: To investigate the impact of periodic decoupling on the performance of NV ensembles in quantum sensing, specifically focusing on dephasing time and sensitivity to magnetic fields.
AI.method: Analyzed the effective inhomogeneous dephasing time using WAHUHA sequences and employed detuning-resolved stroboscopic spectroscopy and finite-pulse Floquet analysis to understand the underlying mechanisms.
AI.result: WAHUHA control increased the effective dephasing time from 0.9 $μ$s to 31 $μ$s without significantly improving dc magnetic-field sensitivity.
AI.conclusion: Extended effective dephasing time under periodic driving does not guarantee enhanced sensitivity, establishing finite-pulse Floquet analysis as a valuable tool for evaluating spin coherence.

title: MATCHA: A Mathematica package for matching UV models onto HEFT
summary: We present MATChing HEFT Amplitudes (MATCHA), a Mathematica package designed for leading-order (LO) matching of an ultraviolet (UV) model to the Higgs Effective Field Theory (HEFT). MATCHA performs the matching of non-decoupling effects $\mathcal{O}(1)$ to the LO HEFT lagrangian for an arbitrary number of Higgs fields. The main benefit of \heftmatcha is that it is built on existing packages such as \texttt{FeynArts} and \texttt{FormCalc}, which are familiar to the user, and directly benefits from the established features of these packages. In addition, \heftmatcha is designed to require minimal input from the user, requiring solely the \texttt{FeynRules} output files and the desired order of expansion. In this way, \heftmatcha provides the leading low-energy couplings capturing non-decoupling effects of HEFT.

AI.tldr: MATCHA is a Mathematica package for leading-order matching of UV models to the Higgs Effective Field Theory (HEFT), focusing on non-decoupling effects in an accessible format.
AI.motivation: The need for a user-friendly tool to perform leading-order matching to HEFT with minimal input requirements, facilitating research in particle physics.
AI.method: MATCHA leverages existing packages like FeynArts and FormCalc, allowing users to input FeynRules output files to obtain low-energy couplings related to non-decoupling effects in HEFT.
AI.result: It successfully matches an arbitrary number of Higgs fields to the LO HEFT lagrangian, providing leading low-energy couplings efficiently.
AI.conclusion: MATCHA enhances usability in HEFT analysis by streamlining the matching process and building upon familiar tools.

title: Single-photon scattering in a dissipative superconducting-qubit--SSH lattice hybrid
summary: We study single-photon scattering in a Su--Schrieffer--Heeger (SSH) photonic lattice locally coupled to a superconducting qubit with tunable loss or gain. Working in the single-excitation sector, we derive an explicit real-space scattering formulation for the full energy-dependent scattering matrix $S(E)$ and identify how its eigenvalues encode coherent perfect absorption, amplification, and spectral singular behavior. The analytical results are benchmarked against time-domain wave-packet simulations, which reproduce the stationary scattering probabilities with high accuracy. We show that the SSH dimerization, the qubit-induced non-Hermitian self-energy, and the synthetic gauge phase cooperate to reshape the reflection and transmission spectra in a highly selective way. In particular, changing the dimerization can switch the system between transmission-dominated and reflection-dominated regimes, while the flux provides a direct handle on interference and symmetry-controlled response. We also find a robust loss--gain correspondence in the reflection landscape and show that the linewidth broadening is governed predominantly by the magnitude $|γ|$ of the non-Hermitian coupling. These results establish a compact and experimentally relevant framework for topological scattering in superconducting quantum networks.

AI.tldr: This paper explores single-photon scattering in a SSH photonic lattice coupled to a superconducting qubit, revealing mechanisms affecting reflection and transmission through the system.
AI.motivation: To understand single-photon interactions in topological photonic systems and their applications in quantum networks.
AI.method: The authors derive a real-space scattering formulation for the energy-dependent scattering matrix $S(E)$ and use time-domain wave-packet simulations for validation.
AI.result: The study identifies how SSH dimerization and qubit coupling influence scattering behaviors, showing a transition between transmission and reflection dominance based on system parameters.
AI.conclusion: This work provides a valuable framework for analyzing topological scattering in superconducting quantum networks and highlights essential phenomena like coherent perfect absorption and loss-gain correspondence.

title: Pulse Modulation as a Signature of the Asteroid-Neutron Star Collision Model for High-Energy Transients
summary: Asteroid-neutron star collision models have been proposed as possible sources of high-energy transients, such as gamma-ray bursts (GRBs) and fast radio bursts (FRBs). The sequence of events following the impact of the asteroid and finally dissolving into the neutron star can have several other observable consequences. We propose that due to the development of the off-diagonal moment of inertia (MI) components, the merger's aftermath can lead to the wobbling of the pulsar (assuming the neutron star happens to be a pulsar). Using sample values of various parameters, viz., size, shape, the locations of the deposits, and the pre-existing pulsar deformation parameter ($η$), we calculate the detailed pulse profile modulation of the pulsar. We observe a distinct pattern of pulse profile modulation on a characteristic timescale enhanced by a factor of $1/η$ compared to the pulse timing. Importantly, even small changes in the MI components, of order $ε$, can produce large pulse profile modulations of order $ε/η$ (depending on the relative location of asteroid material deposition). Thus, if an asteroid-neutron star collision is responsible for a high-energy transient, the associated pulse profile modulation may serve as a falsifiable observational signature of such an event.

AI.tldr: This study suggests that asteroid-neutron star collisions can lead to significant pulse profile modulations in pulsars, providing a testable signature for high-energy transients like GRBs and FRBs.
AI.motivation: Investigate the observable consequences of asteroid-neutron star collisions beyond existing models for high-energy transients, such as GRBs and FRBs.
AI.method: Analyze the effects of the off-diagonal components of moment of inertia in pulsars post-collision and calculate pulse profile modulation based on various parameters.
AI.result: The study finds that small changes in moment of inertia components can lead to pronounced pulse profile modulations, enhanced by the pulsar deformation parameter.
AI.conclusion: The predicted pulse profile modulation serves as a potential observational signature for verifying asteroid-neutron star collision events associated with high-energy transients.

title: Precision measurements at the interface between unitary and non-unitary encoding
summary: We investigate precision scaling at the interface between unitary and non-unitary encoding under generalized noise including single-particle and collective dephasing and decay. Using linear response theory and the error propagation formula, we derive analytic precision expressions for both the unitary parameter $Ω$ and the dissipation strength $γ$. For unitary encoding, when the observable commutes with a Hermitian noise operator, the optimal encoding time is independent of $N$, yielding the Heisenberg limit $ΔΩ\propto 1 / N$; otherwise the precision degrades to the standard quantum limit or ceases to improve with $N$. For non-unitary encoding, when $[\hat{A}, \hat{O}] = 0$, the precision is insensitive to intrinsic dynamics and encoding time, scaling as $Δγ\propto \sqrt{γ/ \expval*{\hat{L}^\dagger \hat{L}}}$. Notably, for collective decay, the Dicke state reaches the Heisenberg limit $Δγ\propto 1 / N$, demonstrating that entanglement can enhance non-unitary estimation. Our results provide a unified framework and practical guidance for designing quantum metrology protocols in noisy environments.

AI.tldr: The paper explores precision scaling in quantum metrology at the crossroad of unitary and non-unitary encoding, particularly under generalized noise conditions, leading to novel insights on optimal encoding times and limits based on system dynamics.
AI.motivation: To understand the impacts of encoding schemes and noise types on precision in quantum metrology, specifically how to maintain or enhance measurement fidelity in noisy environments.
AI.method: Utilizing linear response theory and error propagation formulas to derive precision expressions for unitary and non-unitary parameters under various noise conditions.
AI.result: For unitary encoding, optimal encoding time achieves Heisenberg limit precision independent of particle number under certain conditions. Non-unitary encoding precision is less sensitive to dynamics, with Dicke states achieving Heisenberg limits under collective decay.
AI.conclusion: The study provides a comprehensive framework for improving quantum measurement protocols and informs how to leverage entanglement in non-unitary settings to achieve optimal precision.

title: Non-Hermitian scattering in SSH superconducting waveguides: exact Green-function reduction and dimerization-sensitive microwave functionalities
summary: We formulate an exact Green-function theory for non-Hermitian single-microwave-photon scattering by finite superconducting circuit subsystems embedded in an SSH waveguide. The structured SSH environment is integrated out exactly and enters the local scattering problem as an energy-dependent matrix self-energy, reducing the full open system to a finite-dimensional effective non-Hermitian Hamiltonian. This reduction places scattering amplitudes, exceptional-point diagnostics, coherent-perfect-absorption conditions, and lasing thresholds within one unified framework. Within this approach we analyze two superconducting devices. A flux-controlled two-qubit interferometric scatterer exhibits a broad bright branch and a narrow quasi-dark branch whose interference is reshaped by the SSH environment and changes qualitatively across the two dimerizations. A mediator-assisted two-qubit scatterer generates an additional energy-dependent complex coupling, reorganizes the dressed spectrum, and produces clearer dimerization-sensitive transparency-versus-absorption windows together with a pronounced separation between zero-like and pole-like scattering branches. In the active regime, near-exceptional-point hybridization enhances the pole-dominated response while deepening the singular-value valley associated with near-coherent perfect absorption. These results show how structured topological waveguides can be used not only to host scattering, but also to design non-Hermitian superconducting microwave functionalities.

AI.tldr: The study presents a Green-function theory for non-Hermitian photon scattering in superconducting circuits within an SSH waveguide, creating an effective Hamiltonian to analyze scattering properties and enhance microwave functionalities.
AI.motivation: To investigate non-Hermitian photon scattering dynamics in superconducting circuits integrated into structured environments, focusing on enhanced functionalities and scattering behavior.
AI.method: An exact Green-function theory is formulated, integrating the SSH environment into a matrix self-energy and reducing the system to a finite-dimensional non-Hermitian Hamiltonian.
AI.result: Analyzed two superconducting devices, revealing how the SSH environment reshapes scattering amplitudes and influences behavior, particularly through interference effects and energy-dependent couplings.
AI.conclusion: Structured topological waveguides allow for innovative designs of non-Hermitian superconducting microwave functionalities, leveraging scattering properties and exceptional points.

title: Anomalous mobility edges and extended-localized transition in a quasiperiodic emitter-cavity array
summary: The manipulation of localization in quasiperiodic systems by mobility edges or localization transition holds significant physical importance. In this letter, we demonstrated that the dissipation can induce the emergence of anomalous mobility edges and extended-localized transition in emitter-cavity arrays controlled by quasiperiodic potentials. Specifically, we observe that the localization properties of emitters is governed by the nature of quantum bound states, either discrete or embedded in continuum, providing a unified mechanism linking the emitter-photon bound physics to quasiperiodic criticality. Depending on the bound state discrete or continuumlike, the induced effective excitation hopping exhibits either exponentially decaying or sinusoidally oscillating, giving rise to the formation of localized or critical states, respectively. Through a generalized duality transformation, we analytically determine the anomalous mobility edges and the critical strength of potential, enabling the construction of a full phase diagram. The study reveals that the physical characteristics of cavity exert a significant influence on excitation localization. Therefore, the manipulation of excitation localization can be achieved solely by adjusting the cavity fields.

AI.tldr: This study explores how dissipation influences localization transitions in quasiperiodic systems, revealing a relationship between quantum bound states and emitter localization.
AI.motivation: Understanding how localization in quasiperiodic systems can be manipulated is crucial for future applications in quantum technologies.
AI.method: The authors analyze emitter-cavity arrays influenced by quasiperiodic potentials and employ a duality transformation to investigate mobility edges and localization transitions.
AI.result: They find that the nature of quantum bound states governs localization properties and induces either localized or critical states based on effective excitation hopping behaviors.
AI.conclusion: By tuning cavity fields, one can manipulate excitation localization, highlighting the significant role of cavity characteristics in this process.

title: Equilibrating continuous-variable open quantum systems using stochastic classical trajectories in path-integral space
summary: Beyond the weak-coupling limit, open quantum systems equilibrate to a highly entangled thermal state. For continuous-variable systems, this state can be written explicitly as an imaginary-time phase-space path integral, in which the positions are directly entangled with the bath, and the momenta are correlated with the positions through a phase term. Here, we ask to what extent this state can be reached by propagating stochastic classical trajectories in path-integral phase space. Surprisingly, we find that the trajectories equilibrate to the exact quantum equilibrium state, recovering the purely imaginary momentum-position correlation in the phase term. The trajectories are generated using a recently derived Matsubara generalized Langevin equation, which produces the imaginary correlations by evolving the stochastic variables into the complex plane. This makes the dynamics numerically unstable, but we are nonetheless able to demonstrate the equilibration of a quartic oscillator coupled to a white-noise bath. These unexpected findings could lead to new approximate methodologies for simulating continuous-variable open quantum systems.

AI.tldr: This study explores how classical trajectories in path-integral phase space can reach a highly entangled thermal state in open quantum systems, achieving quantum equilibrium through a novel stochastic process, despite numerical challenges.
AI.motivation: The research aims to bridge classical and quantum descriptions of open quantum systems, particularly focusing on how classical trajectories can replicate quantum behavior in thermal equilibrium.
AI.method: The study employs a Matsubara generalized Langevin equation to derive stochastic classical trajectories in phase space, examining their equilibration to the quantum state.
AI.result: The classical trajectories are shown to equilibrate to the exact quantum equilibrium state, revealing imaginary momentum-position correlations as predicted by quantum theory.
AI.conclusion: These findings suggest potential new approaches to simulating continuous-variable open quantum systems, with implications for computational methodologies.

title: Certification of Network Quantum Sensing
summary:
The distribution of quantum sensors on quantum networks is a key enabler of quantum technologies in interferometry, gravimetry, timekeeping, biological monitoring, and beyond. Yet, guaranteeing the security of these distributed sensors over noisy, insecure networks remains a formidable challenge. Previous efforts to combine quantum metrology and cryptography have encountered an apparently unavoidable tension, proposing bounds for security which are only loosely tied to the achievable measurement performance.
  Here we introduce a quantum remote sensing protocol that can rigorously certify privacy and integrity of the estimation. By employing offline bilateral Pauli-twirling, our approach forces the effective quantum channel into a Bell-diagonal form, independently of the attack. Surprisingly, this also preserves metrological sensitivity without introducing additional experimental overhead. Relying solely on public communication alongside an insecure quantum link, the protocol enables legitimate users to exactly quantify their estimation error relative to an eavesdropper controlling the channels.
  We experimentally demonstrate this framework by estimating an optical phase using entangled photons, observing that the users' precision consistently surpasses the eavesdropper's capabilities across a broad parameter regime. By unifying quantum cryptography and metrology, our results provide a practical pathway to achieve simultaneous quantum-limited precision and rigorous information security in real-world quantum networks.

AI.tldr: A new quantum remote sensing protocol ensures security and precision in quantum networks by combining quantum metrology with cryptography, achieving effective privacy without added overhead.
AI.motivation: To address the challenge of securing distributed quantum sensors over noisy networks, while maintaining measurement performance.
AI.method: A quantum remote sensing protocol utilizing offline bilateral Pauli-twirling to enforce a Bell-diagonal form of the quantum channel with no additional experimental costs.
AI.result: The protocol enabled legitimate users to quantify their estimation error and consistently perform better than an eavesdropper in optical phase estimation with entangled photons.
AI.conclusion: This research merges quantum cryptography and metrology, providing a practical solution for achieving both quantum-limited precision and security in real-world applications.

title: Ultra-high Q-factor superconducting tantalum resonators on 300 mm Si wafers
comment: main text: 11 pages, 4 figures; extended and supplementary: 12 figures and 4 tables
summary: Superconducting resonators are central to superconducting quantum information technologies and essential for bosonic qubit architectures, where long-lived storage modes enable hardware-efficient error correction. Achieving ultra-high quality factors in scalable planar circuits is challenging because multiple dissipation channels contribute to the total loss. Here we report planar $α$-Ta resonators fabricated on 300 mm ultra-high-resistivity ($>10$ k$Ω$ cm) intrinsic silicon using industrial processes, achieving median internal Q factors exceeding 40 million and maxima above 60 million. Energy-participation-ratio analysis identifies a dominant participation-controlled interface loss mechanism and places conservative upper bounds on substrate-associated dissipation. For the best-performing substrate, the inferred substrate loss tangent is below $1.0 \times 10^{-8}$, establishing industrial MCZ silicon among the lowest-loss substrate platforms reported for superconducting resonators. At the same time, the exceptionally low losses show no clear correlation with commonly cited silicon substrate metrics such as room-temperature resistivity or impurity concentrations. More broadly, these studies establish industrial 300 mm processing, careful interface engineering, and 300 mm MCZ silicon substrates as a promising platform for resonator-heavy superconducting quantum architectures with ultra-high quality factors.

AI.tldr: The paper presents planar $α$-Ta superconducting resonators with ultra-high quality factors, fabricated on 300 mm intrinsic silicon. It identifies key loss mechanisms and underscores the potential for scalable qubit architectures.
AI.motivation: To improve superconducting resonators for quantum information technologies and error correction through high-quality factor materials and fabrication processes.
AI.method: The authors fabricated planar $α$-Ta resonators on intrinsic silicon using industrial processes and performed energy-participation-ratio analysis to identify loss mechanisms.
AI.result: The resonators achieved median internal Q factors over 40 million and maxima above 60 million, with substrate loss tangent below $1.0 \times 10^{-8}$, indicating low-loss substrates.
AI.conclusion: The study highlights the viability of using industrial 300 mm MCZ silicon substrates and advanced interface engineering for developing superconducting quantum devices with ultra-high quality factors.

title: Unitary Channel Testing Under a Depolarizing Noise Assumption
summary: We present fast algorithms $\unicode{x2013}$ under the depolarizing noise assumption, often made in fault-tolerant quantum computations $\unicode{x2013}$ to test its strength. Our optimal algorithms answer the following question: is the quantum channel implemented by a given black box identical to a target unitary or $\varepsilon$-far from it in the diamond distance, assuming that the deviation is a depolarizing channel with unknown parameter? Our algorithm has a query complexity of $Θ(1/\varepsilon).$ The query complexity of the relaxed problem of testing whether the black-box channel is $\varepsilon_1$-close to a target unitary or $\varepsilon_2$-far in the diamond distance is $Θ\bigl(\varepsilon_2/(\varepsilon_2 - \varepsilon_1)^2\bigr).$ In both cases, we provide matching lower bounds that hold even for adaptive, ancilla-assisted protocols with multi-outcome incoherent measurements.

AI.tldr: The paper presents efficient algorithms for testing the quality of quantum channels under depolarizing noise, achieving optimal query complexities for distinguishing between target unitaries and deviances.
AI.motivation: To analyze and determine the effectiveness of quantum channels used in fault-tolerant quantum computations, particularly under depolarizing noise.
AI.method: The introduced algorithms measure if a quantum channel matches a target unitary or is significantly different, utilizing diamond distance metrics and offering specific query complexities for different scenarios.
AI.result: The algorithms operate with a query complexity of Θ(1/ε) for direct comparisons and Θ(ε2/(ε2 - ε1)^2) for relaxed conditions with established lower bounds for various testing protocols.
AI.conclusion: These results contribute to understanding the efficiency of quantum channel testing, providing optimal complexities for scenarios commonly encountered in quantum computation.

title: Noise cancellation by superposition of channels and superactivation of quantum capacity: Experimental realization by NMR
summary: Noisy quantum channels degrade quantum resources such as coherence and entanglement and hence pose challenges for realizing quantum technologies. Coherent control of noisy channels allows us to minimize their effects on the quantum system. Here we achieve the cancellation of two noisy quantum channels by superposing their corresponding Stinespring dilation unitaries. We first arrive at conditions under which superposition of channels results in a valid quantum channel. We then consider superposing two dephasing channels and observe their destructive interference, thereby effectively recovering the quantum coherence. On superposing two zero-capacity depolarizing channels, we show superactivation of quantum capacity. We experimentally realize the cancellation of two dephasing channels using a three-qubit NMR register. Furthermore, using a five-qubit NMR register, we realize the cancellation of two depolarization channels and demonstrate superactivation of quantum capacity.

AI.tldr: The paper reports on the cancellation of noisy quantum channels through coherent control and superposition, enabling the recovery of quantum coherence and superactivation of quantum capacity in experimental setups.
AI.motivation: To address the degradation of quantum resources like coherence and entanglement in noisy quantum channels, enhancing the reliability of quantum technologies.
AI.method: Superposing Stinespring dilation unitaries of two noisy channels and analyzing conditions for their valid superposition, followed by experimental realization using NMR registers.
AI.result: Destructive interference was observed in dephasing channels, recovering coherence; superactivation of quantum capacity was demonstrated with depolarizing channels.
AI.conclusion: This study highlights coherent control methods that can mitigate noise in quantum systems, paving the way for more reliable quantum technologies.

title: The fidelity of controlled quantum teleportation in a noisy environment
summary: In this work, we investigate controlled quantum teleportation in the presence of noisy channels acting on the three-qubit resource state. We employ a series of generalized noisy channels that bridge the dephasing channels and amplitude damping channels while encompassing extensive intermediate scenarios. We provide an in-depth analysis of the degradation of the maximal average fidelity and the optimal average fidelity in controlled quantum teleportation induced by such noisy channels by deriving the analytical expression and examining several special cases. The analytical expression shows that attaining the optimal average fidelity requires Charlie's cooperation in performing a measurement at suitably chosen angles, and is also related to the initial state and the channel parameters. Our analysis reveals that the optimal average fidelity does not always decrease monotonically with the evolution parameter, instead, it first decreases and then increases. This non-monotonic behavior depends on the entanglement of the initial resource state, as well as on the parameters of the channel traversed by the first qubit.

AI.tldr: This study analyzes controlled quantum teleportation affected by noisy channels, revealing non-monotonic changes in fidelity based on channel parameters and initial entanglement.
AI.motivation: To understand how noisy channels impact controlled quantum teleportation and maximize fidelity in such scenarios.
AI.method: The authors derive analytical expressions and investigate various noisy channels, focusing on their effects on fidelity in controlled teleportation.
AI.result: The study finds that optimal fidelity depends on measurement angles, initial states, and channel parameters, exhibiting non-monotonic behavior influenced by the initial resource state's entanglement.
AI.conclusion: To achieve optimal average fidelity in controlled quantum teleportation, cooperation from Charlie is essential, and fidelity behavior can exhibit unexpected increases after initial decreases.

title: Sensitivity Enhancement near High-Order Exceptional Points via Dissipative Couplings
summary: High-order exceptional points (EPs) emerging in non-Hermitian systems have attracted broad interest for their significantly enhanced sensitivity to perturbations. However, quantum sensing schemes based on high-order EPs remain scarce, due to the experimental challenge of fine-tuning the system to such an extremely sensitive isolated point. Here we propose a four-channel dissipative coupling model that supports both fourth-order exceptional surfaces and second-order exceptional volumes. This non-Hermitian model can be realized in a thermal atomic system, and its complex energy spectra can be determined via electromagnetically induced transparency spectroscopy. The proposed model exhibits a characteristic fourth-order response to multiple physical quantities such as the laser detuning and the distance between optical channels, significantly surpassing the response of second-order EPs. We further reveal the sensitivity-robustness trade-off under experimental noise. Our work opens a route toward high-performance sensing leveraging higher-order EPs.

AI.tldr: The paper proposes a model for utilizing high-order exceptional points in non-Hermitian systems for improved quantum sensing.
AI.motivation: High-order EPs have enhanced sensitivity to perturbations, but practical quantum sensing schemes are limited by the difficulty of achieving precise tuning to these points.
AI.method: A four-channel dissipative coupling model is introduced, enabling exploration of fourth-order exceptional surfaces and second-order exceptional volumes, applicable in thermal atomic systems and analyzed via electromagnetically induced transparency spectroscopy.
AI.result: The model demonstrates a significantly enhanced fourth-order response to variables like laser detuning and optical channel distances, outperforming second-order EP responses.
AI.conclusion: This approach presents a pathway for advanced sensing technologies by leveraging high-order exceptional points, addressing the sensitivity-robustness balance under noise.

title: Quantum Colorings of Spheres
summary: Cameron, Montanaro, Newman, Severini and Winter gave a construction which shows that, for $n \in \{2,4,8\}$, any graph $G$ which admits a real $n$-dimensional orthogonal representation is quantumly $n$-colorable. This result can be recast as the statement that the real sphere $S^{n-1}$ is quantumly $n$-colorable for these values of $n$. We investigate possible extensions of their construction. We first show that their hypothesis that the orthogonal representation be real-valued is required by proving that there is no analogue of this for the complex spheres, which all have quantum chromatic number strictly bigger than the dimension except in two dimensions. We also provide candidate finitary witnesses of this and show for the first time that the real and complex orthogonal ranks are distinct as a byproduct. For the real case, we show that if $S^{n-1}$ is quantumly $n$-colorable, then either $n=2$ or $n$ is a multiple of 4, and show that the converse holds whenever a Hadamard matrix of order $n$ exists. Hence, assuming the Hadamard conjecture, this completely classifies the dimensions to which the CMNSW construction can be extended. Our method of proof involves showing the equivalence between the existence of such a construction and the existence of a maximal code space for Clifford-algebraic errors given a clean ancilla, and we believe that the representation-theoretic techniques we use for tackling the latter problem could be of independent interest. It also follows from this equivalence that $S^{n-1}$ admits a rank-one quantum $n$-coloring if and only if $n \in \{2,4,8\}$, thereby settling a conjecture of Zeng and Zhang, as does the fact that for all $m \geq 1$, there exists a catalytic zero-error remote state preparation protocol for real $m$-qubit states with $m$ bits of communication and which consumes $m$ ebits.

AI.tldr: This paper extends the work of Cameron et al. by exploring the bounds and cases for quantum colorability of spheres based on orthogonal representations, proving distinctions between real and complex cases, and classifying dimensions under the Hadamard conjecture.
AI.motivation: To explore the extensions of the construction by Cameron et al. regarding quantum colorability in relation to orthogonal representations and to clarify the distinction between real and complex quantum chromatic numbers.
AI.method: The authors prove the necessity of real orthogonal representations, show the implications of Hadamard matrices, and establish equivalences relating representation theory to quantum colorability.
AI.result: They find that real spheres can only be quantumly n-colorable if n=2 or n is a multiple of 4, and they classify dimensions under the Hadamard conjecture concerning quantum colorability.
AI.conclusion: Their findings resolve existing conjectures and suggest that representation-theoretic techniques may have broader applications in quantum information theory.

title: Genuine Multipartite Nonlocality for Arbitrary Input: Maximal Randomness Generation and Robust Self-Testing
summary: Bell nonlocality provides the foundation for device-independent (DI) certification of quantum devices. We introduce a Bell inequality capable of identifying genuine multipartite nonlocality (GMNL) in an arbitrary m-partite scenario with an arbitrary odd number of measurements per party. Since the multi-setting nature of this inequality precludes the use of Jordan's Lemma, we construct an analytical sum-of-squares (SOS) decomposition to obtain the optimal quantum violation without assuming any bound on the Hilbert space dimension. This, in turn, enables self-testing of the shared entangled state and the corresponding measurement observables, up to local isometries, whose existence we confirm using a swap-based certification scheme. In addition, we show that our framework enables the extraction of maximal global DI randomness (m bits) at the optimal quantum violation, thereby exceeding previous limitations in the GMNL regime. Finally, we demonstrate that the architecture of our inequality yields improved robustness to noise as the number of measurement settings grows, ensuring experimental feasibility.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a Bell inequality for genuine multipartite nonlocality, providing methods for optimal quantum violation without dimensional constraints, enhancing device-independent randomness, and improving robustness to noise with increased measurement settings.
AI.motivation: To advance the certification of quantum devices using Bell nonlocality, particularly in multipartite scenarios under realistic conditions.
AI.method: A Bell inequality is constructed using an analytical SOS decomposition, enabling optimal quantum violation without assuming any bound on Hilbert space dimensions. It incorporates a swap-based certification scheme for entangled states and measurement observables.
AI.result: The proposed inequality demonstrates optimal quantum violation, allowing self-testing of entangled states and enabling extraction of m bits of global device-independent randomness, surpassing previous bounds in GMNL.
AI.conclusion: The framework enhances robustness to noise as the number of measurement settings increases, ensuring the practical applicability of the findings in experimental settings.

title: Inherent flux crosstalk and coupler-driven single-qubit gates in superconducting circuits
summary: Crosstalk refers to unwanted qubit addressing. This is particularly detrimental when scaling up quantum information systems because unintended interactions limit their overall performance. For superconducting qubits, tunable couplings and frequency tunability achieved through externally applied magnetic fluxes enable high-fidelity entangling gates; however, they also introduce crosstalk through unintended flux coupling. In this work, we investigate the impact of time-dependent external magnetic fluxes in quantized circuits on superconducting qubit couplings. We find that non-trivial cross-voltage driving emerges between capacitively linked qubits when the magnetic flux threading the SQUID loop of a qubit varies in time, in a manner analogous to Faraday's law of induction. Crucially, we show that this effect enables fast single qubit control through the coupler element in standard tunable-coupler architectures, potentially eliminating the need for individual microwave $XY$ control lines.

AI.tldr: This paper explores the impact of time-dependent magnetic flux on crosstalk in superconducting qubits, revealing a method for improved qubit control, potentially reducing the need for separate control lines.
AI.motivation: To address crosstalk issues in superconducting qubits which hinder the performance of quantum information systems as they scale.
AI.method: The investigation focuses on the effects of varying external magnetic fluxes on couplings between qubits in quantized circuits, drawing parallels to Faraday's law of induction.
AI.result: The study finds that variable magnetic fluxes induce non-trivial cross-voltage driving in capacitively linked qubits, enhancing qubit control through the coupler.
AI.conclusion: This method could facilitate faster single qubit control in tunable-coupler architectures, reducing the complexity of control systems in quantum circuits.

title: Robust self-testing based on Gisin's arbitrary-input Bell inequality
comment: arXiv admin note: substantial text overlap with arXiv:2505.19917
summary: Self-testing refers to the strongest device-independent (DI) certification method that validates the nature of a quantum system and devices solely based on the observed statistics. We demonstrate the self-testing of state and measurements based on the Gisin Bell inequality (GBI) featuring arbitrary inputs for both parties. We introduce a systematic and elegant sum-of-squares (SOS) approach that enables the dimension-independent derivation of the optimal quantum violation of GBI. We derive the state and the interrelation between the local observables directly from the optimization condition. Since the practical experimental scenario involves inevitable noise and imperfection, we present a comprehensive strategy for robust self-testing.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a self-testing method for quantum systems based on the Gisin Bell inequality, featuring a systematic sum-of-squares approach and addressing noise in practical implementations.
AI.motivation: The paper addresses the need for robust device-independent certification methods in quantum systems, focusing on reliable validation despite experimental imperfections.
AI.method: The authors utilize a sum-of-squares approach to derive the optimal quantum violation of the Gisin Bell inequality, providing dimension-independent results and deriving local observables.
AI.result: The paper successfully derives the optimal violation of the Gisin Bell inequality and establishes the interrelation between states and local observables under the optimization conditions.
AI.conclusion: The proposed robust self-testing strategy enhances the reliability of quantum certification in practical experimental scenarios with noise.
